```typescript
// illuminate as a Claude Code channel: an MCP server Claude Code starts over stdio, so the person's own Claude Code
// session does the reading and writing (on their own sign-in) instead of a separate Agent SDK session with its own key.
//
// The local illuminate server runs inside this process with a bridge `Agent` (bridge.ts). Work reaches Claude two ways:
// - in tool results: `illuminate_map` and `illuminate_submit` wait briefly for the next request, so making a map
//   (draft, check, repair) runs within one turn;
// - as a channel message, when work starts from the browser (a question on the map, New map) and no tool call is
//   waiting. Claude then calls `illuminate_next`.
// Only the person's browser can start work, and the page needs illuminate's token, so the channel is gated.
// Channels are a Claude Code research preview: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference
import * as fs from 'node:fs';
import * as path from 'node:path';
import { Server } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js';
import { CallToolRequestSchema, ListToolsRequestSchema, type ServerNotification } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/types.js';
import { createBridge, type Bridge, type BridgeRequest } from './bridge';
import { openBrowser } from './browser';
import { startServer, type IlluminateServer, type ServerEvent } from './server';
import { createStore } from './store';

export type ChannelOptions = {
  /** The repo maps are about unless a tool call names another (Claude Code passes CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR). */
  root: string;
  /** How a link is opened in the browser (tests pass a no-op). */
  open?: (url: string) => void;
  /** How long a tool call waits for the next piece of work before handing the turn back (default 90 s). */
  waitMs?: number;
  /** Port for the local server (default 4317, or the next free one). */
  port?: number;
};

export const CHANNEL_INSTRUCTIONS = [
  'illuminate draws checked, interactive maps of how this codebase works, in the person\'s browser. You do the reading and writing; illuminate checks every claim against the code before it shows anything.',
  '- When the person asks how something works across files ("what happens when…", "how does X reach Y") or asks for a map, diagram or walkthrough, call illuminate_map with their question in their own words.',
  '- illuminate gives you work as requests, in tool results or announced by a <channel source="illuminate" request_id="..."> message (call illuminate_next to get it). Each request says what to do and the JSON to return. Explore the code with Read, Grep and Glob, then call illuminate_submit with the request_id and your output. If the result holds another request, do that one too. If you can\'t finish one, call illuminate_fail.',
  '- While working on an illuminate request, don\'t edit files or run commands that change anything, and never read secret files (.env, keys). A fix is only proposed; illuminate applies it after the person approves it on the map.',
  '- Answers are shown on the map. In the terminal, say at most a sentence or two.',
].join('\n');

const TOOLS = [
  {
    name: 'illuminate_map',
    description: 'Make a checked map that answers a question about how this codebase works, and open it in the person\'s browser. Returns the first piece of work for you to do.',
    inputSchema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        question: { type: 'string', description: 'The person\'s question, in their own words.' },
        repo: { type: 'string', description: 'The repo root, if not the project Claude Code was started in.' },
      },
      required: ['question'],
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'illuminate_next',
    description: 'Get the next piece of work illuminate has for you (after an illuminate channel message).',
    inputSchema: { type: 'object', properties: {} },
  },
  {
    name: 'illuminate_submit',
    description: 'Hand in your output for an illuminate request. It is checked; if it can\'t be read you get the problems back to fix. Returns the next piece of work, if there is one.',
    inputSchema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        request_id: { type: 'string' },
        output: { type: 'object', description: 'JSON matching the request\'s schema.' },
      },
      required: ['request_id', 'output'],
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'illuminate_fail',
    description: 'Give up on an illuminate request, saying why in plain words. The person sees it on the map.',
    inputSchema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: { request_id: { type: 'string' }, reason: { type: 'string' } },
      required: ['request_id', 'reason'],
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'illuminate_open',
    description: 'Open saved maps in the person\'s browser: one map, or the list of all of them. Returns the maps saved in the repo.',
    inputSchema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        map_id: { type: 'string', description: 'A saved map\'s id; leave out for the list.' },
        repo: { type: 'string' },
      },
    },
  },
] as const;

/** A request as Claude reads it: what it's for, how to answer, the prompt, and the output schema. */
export function requestText(r: BridgeRequest): string {
  return [
    `## illuminate request ${r.id}: ${r.label}`,
    '',
    `When you're done, call illuminate_submit with request_id "${r.id}" and \`output\`: a JSON object matching the schema at the end. Don't edit any files.`,
    r.tools.length ? '' : 'Answer from what is in this request alone. Don\'t read the code for this one.',
    r.continues ? 'This follows on from your earlier work for illuminate in this conversation.' : '',
    '',
    '---',
    r.prompt,
    '---',
    '',
    '## Output schema (JSON Schema)',
    JSON.stringify(r.schema),
  ].filter((line, i, all) => line !== '' || all[i - 1] !== '').join('\n');
}

type Text = { content: { type: 'text'; text: string }[]; isError?: boolean };
const text = (t: string, isError = false): Text => ({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: t }], ...(isError ? { isError } : {}) });

export function createChannel(o: ChannelOptions) {
  const open = o.open ?? openBrowser;
  const waitMs = o.waitMs ?? 90_000;
  const servers = new Map<string, Promise<IlluminateServer>>();
  /** Listeners for "something finished", so a waiting tool call can say so. */
  const finished = new Set<(message: string) => void>();
  const lastReport = new Map<string, { confirmed: number; claims: number }>();

  const mcp = new Server(
    { name: 'illuminate', version: '0.1.0' },
    { capabilities: { experimental: { 'claude/channel': {} }, tools: {} }, instructions: CHANNEL_INSTRUCTIONS },
  );

  const bridge: Bridge = createBridge({
    announce: (r) => {
      void mcp
        .notification({
          method: 'notifications/claude/channel',
          params: { content: `illuminate has work for you: ${r.label}. Call illuminate_next to get it.`, meta: { request_id: r.id } },
        } as unknown as ServerNotification)
        .catch(() => {});
    },
  });

  const rootOf = (repo: unknown): string => {
    const dir = path.resolve(o.root, typeof repo === 'string' && repo.trim() ? repo : '.');
    if (!fs.existsSync(dir) || !fs.statSync(dir).isDirectory()) throw new Error(`No such folder: ${dir}`);
    return fs.realpathSync(dir);
  };

  const serverFor = (root: string): Promise<IlluminateServer> => {
    let s = servers.get(root);
    if (!s) {
      s = startServer({
        root,
        port: o.port ?? 4317,
        agent: bridge.agent,
        // The Stop button stops the page's server; the next illuminate tool call starts a new one.
        onStop: () => servers.delete(root),
        onEvent: (e) => void onEvent(root, e),
      });
      s.catch(() => servers.delete(root));
      servers.set(root, s);
    }
    return s;
  };

  async function onEvent(root: string, e: ServerEvent) {
    if (e.type === 'map') lastReport.set(e.mapId, { confirmed: e.report.summary.confirmed, claims: e.report.summary.claims });
    if (e.type !== 'job' || e.status === 'started') return;
    let message: string;
    if (e.status === 'failed') message = `illuminate couldn't finish "${e.question}": ${e.error ?? 'unknown error'}`;
    else if (e.job === 'make') {
      const s = await servers.get(root);
      const r = lastReport.get(e.mapId);
      message = [
        `The map for "${e.question}" is ready${r ? `: ${r.confirmed} of ${r.claims} claims confirmed against the code` : ''}.`,
        s ? `It's open in the browser: ${s.pageUrl(e.mapId)}` : '',
        'Tell the person in a sentence; the map does the explaining. They can take the walkthrough, or select any box and ask about it there.',
      ].filter(Boolean).join('\n');
    } else message = `The answer to "${e.question}" is shown on the map.`;
    for (const f of [...finished]) f(message);
  }

  /** After handing something in: the next request, or what finished, or (after a while) that nothing is needed yet. */
  async function whatNext(): Promise<Text> {
    const ac = new AbortController();
    let onFinish: ((m: string) => void) | null = null;
    const done = new Promise<string>((resolve) => {
      onFinish = resolve;
      finished.add(resolve);
    });
    const timer = new Promise<null>((resolve) => setTimeout(() => resolve(null), waitMs).unref?.());
    try {
      const winner = await Promise.race([
        bridge.waitForNext(ac.signal).then((r) => (r ? { request: r } : null)),
        done.then((message) => ({ message })),
        timer,
      ]);
      if (winner && 'request' in winner) return text(requestText(winner.request));
      if (winner && 'message' in winner) return text(winner.message);
      return text('illuminate is still working on its side. If it needs you, an illuminate channel message will say so.');
    } finally {
      ac.abort();
      if (onFinish) finished.delete(onFinish);
    }
  }

  mcp.setRequestHandler(ListToolsRequestSchema, async () => ({ tools: TOOLS.map((t) => ({ ...t })) as never }));

  mcp.setRequestHandler(CallToolRequestSchema, async (req): Promise<Text> => {
    const args = (req.params.arguments ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
    try {
      switch (req.params.name) {
        case 'illuminate_map': {
          const question = String(args.question ?? '').trim();
          if (!question) return text('Pass the person\'s question.', true);
          const server = await serverFor(rootOf(args.repo));
          // Listen before starting, so neither the first request nor an early failure is missed.
          const next = whatNext();
          const id = server.startMap(question);
          const url = server.pageUrl(id);
          open(url);
          const first = await next;
          return { ...first, content: [{ type: 'text', text: `The map is opening in the browser: ${url}\nTell the person, and give them the link in case the tab didn't appear.\n` }, ...first.content] };
        }
        case 'illuminate_next': {
          const r = bridge.next();
          return text(r ? requestText(r) : 'Nothing is waiting right now.');
        }
        case 'illuminate_submit': {
          const id = String(args.request_id ?? '');
          const next = whatNext();
          const r = bridge.submit(id, args.output);
          if (!r.ok) {
            void next;
            return text(`That output for ${id} can't be used yet. Fix these and call illuminate_submit again:\n${r.problems.map((p) => `- ${p}`).join('\n')}`, true);
          }
          return await next;
        }
        case 'illuminate_fail': {
          const ok = bridge.fail(String(args.request_id ?? ''), String(args.reason ?? 'no reason given'));
          return text(ok ? 'Told the person on the map.' : 'No such request is waiting.');
        }
        case 'illuminate_open': {
          const root = rootOf(args.repo);
          const server = await serverFor(root);
          const mapId = typeof args.map_id === 'string' && args.map_id ? args.map_id : undefined;
          const url = server.pageUrl(mapId);
          open(url);
          const maps = createStore(root).list();
          return text([`Opened ${url}`, '', maps.length ? 'Saved maps:' : 'No maps saved in this repo yet.', ...maps.map((m) => `${m.id}  ${m.question}`)].join('\n'));
        }
        default:
          return text(`Unknown tool: ${req.params.name}`, true);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      return text(err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err), true);
    }
  });

  return {
    mcp,
    bridge,
    async close() {
      for (const s of servers.values()) await s.then((x) => x.close()).catch(() => {});
      servers.clear();
      await mcp.close();
    },
  };
}
```

```bash
/** `illume channel`: serve the channel over stdio until Claude Code closes it. stdout belongs to MCP, so logs go to stderr. */
```

```text
// The local server end to end over HTTP and WebSocket, with a scripted Claude: make a map, ask, approve a fix, undo.
import * as http from 'node:http';
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import WebSocket from 'ws';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { startServer, type IlluminateServer, type ServerEvent } from '../src/server';
import { CARE_MAP, LISTENER_FIX, cleanup, copyCareApp, scriptedAgent, waitFor } from './helpers';

let server: IlluminateServer;
let root: string;
const events: ServerEvent[] = [];
let ws: WebSocket;

const agent = scriptedAgent([
  () => CARE_MAP,
  // First question: the map-only try says it needs the code, then Claude answers with it.
  () => ({ route: 'code', missing: 'Who listens for the announcement.' }),
  () => ({ concept: 'Nothing listens for the announcement, so the rules never run from here.', refs: ['miss'], moves: { focus: 's4', highlight: ['s4', 'miss'] } }),
  // Second: a change request always needs the code.
  () => ({ route: 'code', missing: 'The change itself.' }),
  () => ({ concept: 'Add a listener.', refs: ['miss'], fix: LISTENER_FIX }),
]);

const api = async (method: string, path: string, body?: unknown, headers: Record<string, string> = {}) => {
  const res = await fetch(`${server.url}${path}`, {
    method,
    headers: { 'x-illuminate-token': server.token, 'content-type': 'application/json', ...headers },
    body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
  });
  return { status: res.status, body: (await res.json()) as any };
};

beforeAll(async () => {
  root = copyCareApp();
  server = await startServer({ root, port: 0, agent, viewerDir: join(root, 'no-viewer') });
  ws = new WebSocket(`ws://127.0.0.1:${server.port}/ws?t=${server.token}`);
  ws.on('message', (d) => events.push(JSON.parse(String(d))));
  await new Promise((r) => ws.once('open', r));
});
afterAll(async () => {
  ws.close();
  await server.close();
  cleanup();
});

describe('the illuminate server', () => {
  let mapId = '';

  it('makes a map from a question and streams progress', async () => {
    const r = await api('POST', '/api/maps', { question: 'What happens when a patient converts?' });
    expect(r).toEqual({ status: 202, body: { id: 'patient-converts' } });
    mapId = r.body.id;
    await waitFor(() => events.find((e) => e.type === 'job' && e.job === 'make' && e.status === 'done'));
    expect(events.filter((e) => e.type === 'progress').map((e) => (e as { text: string }).text)).toEqual(
      expect.arrayContaining(['Scanning the code for ways in, routes and tables', 'Reading src/patients/service.ts', '15 of 15 claims confirmed']),
    );
    const got = await api('GET', `/api/maps/${mapId}`);
    expect(got.body.report.summary).toEqual({ claims: 15, confirmed: 15, unconfirmed: 0 });
    expect(existsSync(join(root, '.illuminate/maps/patient-converts.json'))).toBe(true);
```

```typescript
// illuminate as a Claude Code channel, driven the way Claude Code drives it: an MCP client calls the tools, and the
// test plays Claude by submitting output. No model is called.
import { Client } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js';
import { InMemoryTransport } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/inMemory.js';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { createBridge } from '../src/bridge';
import { createChannel } from '../src/channel';
import { MAP_SCHEMA } from '../src/schemas';
import { CARE_MAP, cleanup, copyCareApp, waitFor } from './helpers';

describe('the bridge', () => {
  it('announces a request when nothing is waiting, and hands back output once it reads', async () => {
    const announced: string[] = [];
    const bridge = createBridge({ announce: (r) => announced.push(r.id) });
    const reply = bridge.agent({ prompt: 'Draw it', label: 'Making a map', schema: MAP_SCHEMA, cwd: '/' });
    expect(announced).toEqual(['r1']);
    expect(bridge.next()).toMatchObject({ id: 'r1', label: 'Making a map', continues: false });

    const bad = bridge.submit('r1', { version: 1 });
    expect(bad.ok).toBe(false);
    expect(bridge.submit('r1', JSON.stringify(CARE_MAP))).toEqual({ ok: true });
    await expect(reply).resolves.toMatchObject({ output: CARE_MAP, sessionId: 'claude-code', cost: null });
    expect(bridge.outstanding()).toEqual([]);
    expect(bridge.submit('r1', CARE_MAP).ok).toBe(false);
  });

  it('hands a request to a waiting tool call instead of announcing it, and lets Claude give up', async () => {
    const announced: string[] = [];
    const bridge = createBridge({ announce: (r) => announced.push(r.id) });
    const ac = new AbortController();
    const waiting = bridge.waitForNext(ac.signal);
    const reply = bridge.agent({ prompt: 'Answer', schema: MAP_SCHEMA, cwd: '/', tools: [], resume: 'claude-code' });
    await expect(waiting).resolves.toMatchObject({ id: 'r1', tools: [], continues: true });
    expect(announced).toEqual([]);
    expect(bridge.fail('r1', 'the code is not there')).toBe(true);
    await expect(reply).rejects.toThrow('the code is not there');
  });

  it('drops a waiting tool call once it stops listening', async () => {
    const announced: string[] = [];
    const bridge = createBridge({ announce: (r) => announced.push(r.id) });
    const ac = new AbortController();
    const waiting = bridge.waitForNext(ac.signal);
    ac.abort();
    await expect(waiting).resolves.toBeNull();
    void bridge.agent({ prompt: 'x', schema: MAP_SCHEMA, cwd: '/' }).catch(() => {});
    expect(announced).toEqual(['r1']);
  });
});

describe('the channel', () => {
  let root: string;
  let client: Client;
  let channel: ReturnType<typeof createChannel>;
  const opened: string[] = [];
  const pushed: { content: string; meta: Record<string, string> }[] = [];
  const call = async (name: string, args: Record<string, unknown> = {}) => {
    const r = (await client.callTool({ name, arguments: args })) as { content: { text: string }[]; isError?: boolean };
    return { text: r.content.map((c) => c.text).join('\n'), isError: !!r.isError };
  };
  const requestId = (text: string) => /illuminate request (r\d+)/.exec(text)?.[1] ?? '';

  beforeAll(async () => {
    root = copyCareApp();
    channel = createChannel({ root, port: 0, open: (u) => opened.push(u), waitMs: 5000 });
    client = new Client({ name: 'claude-code-stand-in', version: '0' });
    client.fallbackNotificationHandler = async (n) => {
      if (n.method === 'notifications/claude/channel') pushed.push(n.params as (typeof pushed)[number]);
    };
    const [a, b] = InMemoryTransport.createLinkedPair();
    await Promise.all([channel.mcp.connect(b), client.connect(a)]);
  });
  afterAll(async () => {
    await client.close();
    await channel.close();
    cleanup();
  });

  it('tells Claude Code it is a channel with tools, and how to use them', async () => {
    expect(client.getServerCapabilities()?.experimental).toHaveProperty('claude/channel');
    expect(client.getInstructions()).toContain('illuminate_submit');
    const { tools } = await client.listTools();
    expect(tools.map((t) => t.name)).toEqual(['illuminate_map', 'illuminate_next', 'illuminate_submit', 'illuminate_fail', 'illuminate_open']);
  });

  let mapUrl = '';
  it('makes a map in one turn: the first request comes back from illuminate_map, the result from illuminate_submit', async () => {
    const first = await call('illuminate_map', { question: 'What happens when a patient converts?' });
    expect(first.isError).toBe(false);
    expect(opened).toHaveLength(1);
    mapUrl = opened[0]!;
    expect(first.text).toContain(mapUrl);
    expect(first.text).toContain('Making the map for "What happens when a patient converts?"');
    expect(first.text).toContain('## Output schema');
    const id = requestId(first.text);

    const wrong = await call('illuminate_submit', { request_id: id, output: { version: 1 } });
    expect(wrong.isError).toBe(true);
    expect(wrong.text).toContain('Fix these');

    const done = await call('illuminate_submit', { request_id: id, output: CARE_MAP });
    expect(done.text).toContain('15 of 15 claims confirmed');
    expect(done.text).toContain(mapUrl.split('?')[0]);
    expect(pushed).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('pushes a question asked on the map into the session, and the answer goes back to the map', async () => {
    const url = new URL(mapUrl);
    const mapId = url.pathname.split('/').pop()!;
    const res = await fetch(`${url.origin}/api/maps/${mapId}/ask`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'x-illuminate-token': url.searchParams.get('t')!, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ question: 'Why does no email go out?' }),
    });
    expect(res.status).toBe(202);
    await waitFor(() => pushed.length > 0);
    expect(pushed[0]).toMatchObject({ meta: { request_id: expect.stringMatching(/^r\d+$/) } });
    expect(pushed[0]!.content).toContain('Answering "Why does no email go out?" from the map');

    const req = await call('illuminate_next');
    expect(req.text).toContain('Answer from what is in this request alone');
    const done = await call('illuminate_submit', {
      request_id: requestId(req.text),
      output: { route: 'answer', concept: 'Nothing listens for the announcement, so the rules never run.', refs: ['miss'] },
    });
    expect(done.text).toContain('is shown on the map');

    const saved = await (await fetch(`${url.origin}/api/maps/${mapId}`, { headers: { 'x-illuminate-token': url.searchParams.get('t')! } })).json() as { answers: { concept: string }[] };
    expect(saved.answers.at(-1)?.concept).toContain('Nothing listens');
  });

  it('opens saved maps and lists them', async () => {
    const r = await call('illuminate_open');
    expect(r.text).toContain('patient-converts  What happens when a patient converts?');
    expect(await call('illuminate_next')).toMatchObject({ text: 'Nothing is waiting right now.' });
  });
});
```

````text
# illuminate

Ask how your code works and get a map you can point at. Claude explores the repo and drafts the answer as a graph of
areas, steps and labeled arrows. A plain program checks every box and arrow against the real code before you see it.
Then you can take a walkthrough, select any part and ask about it, and fix a missing connection right from the map.

Design: [Codemap v1 Design](https://claude.ai/artifact/55L8tokprGe61qtfpDXJ5h).

## Use it

```
npm i
npm run build                                              # the viewer
npm run illume -- "What happens when a user signs up?" --repo /path/to/your/repo
```

It prints a link (`http://127.0.0.1:4317/m/<id>?t=<token>`) and opens it. illuminate stops on its own about 30 seconds after
you close its last tab (never while Claude is working), or when you press Stop illuminate on the page. Maps are saved in the target repo under
`.illuminate/maps/`; commit them to share. Other commands:

```
npm run illume -- open --repo <dir>            # maps already made in that repo
npm run illume -- check <map-id> --repo <dir>  # re-check a saved map against the code (exit 1 if a claim fails)
```

Options: `--port <n>` (default 4317), `--no-open`, `--model <id>` (default `claude-opus-5-5`, or `ILLUMINATE_MODEL`).

Claude access: an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or a logged-in Claude Code (the Agent SDK uses it). To keep the key in a file,
`cp .env.example .env` at the root of this checkout and fill it in; the CLI loads it, and your shell's variables win.

To put `illuminate` on your PATH: `npm link -w @illuminate/server`.

### From a coding agent

`integrations/skills/illuminate/SKILL.md` is a skill in the standard `SKILL.md` format. Copy the `illuminate` folder into
`.claude/skills/` (Claude Code), `.agents/skills/` (Codex, Gemini CLI) or `.cursor/skills/` (Cursor). Your agent then
runs illuminate when you ask how something works, and hands you the link.

### Try it without a model

```
npm run preview
```

The real server and viewer on a throwaway copy of the care-app fixture, with a scripted stand-in for Claude. Nothing
````

```text
## 5. Design decisions and why

1. **v1: Claude explores, a plain program checks.** No deterministic graph engine yet, because it isn't needed for
   "ask, get a map". Claude explores with Read/Grep/Glob and returns the map in a fixed format. `check()` re-reads every
   cited line and verifies calls, requests and imports against code facts. Later, the engine can replace the explorer
   behind the same format.
2. **The map format (`packages/core/src/format.ts`) is the one-way door.** Everything else is replaceable. Statuses are
   never stored; they're computed on every check.
3. **"Nothing does X" is a claim with proof.** Absences carry the search that proves them, and the checker reruns it.
   The missing connection is the bug people care about, and only a graph that can show absences can show it.
4. **Illuminate runs its own Claude explainer,** separate from the user's coding chat. It works with any agent and keeps
   explanation quality consistent. It can read the whole repo: the map is a starting point, not a fence. Anything it
   adds is drawn only if the checker confirms it.
5. **Fixes:** Claude proposes. The fix is drawn as a green dashed arrow next to the exact diff. Nothing changes until
   approval. Then illuminate writes exactly that diff, refusing if the files changed since the proposal, re-checks the map,
   and offers Undo. Only one agent edits at a time. If illuminate is ever connected to the user's coding chat, that agent
   makes the edit instead.
6. **Delivery:** the basic version works everywhere through a skill, the `illume` CLI and a browser tab. Optional
## 7. What's built (verified)

- **Tests:** four packages, 102 tests, no model calls.
- **Viewer:** tested in Chrome with scripted Claude (`npm run preview`): making a map, the walkthrough, select and ask,
  a follow-up that adds checked steps, a fix (approve, reload, undo).
- **Real Claude, on the care-app fixture:**
  - The map came back 20 of 20 confirmed on the first pass, for about $0.21.
  - It also found a bug nobody planted: nothing ever starts the nightly job.
  - A real question cost about $0.14 and added two confirmed gaps.
  - A real fix cost about $0.24, was approved and applied, and re-checked 22 of 22.
- **Demo frontend:** `examples/care-app-ui/index.html`, the patient app as staff see it. Convert a patient and no welcome
  email arrives, even though the automation is active.

## 8. Not built yet, and next steps

- **Undo for an applied fix lasts only while the server runs.** Questions, answers and fix states are saved with the
  map (since 2026-11-03), and simple questions are answered from the map before Claude searches the code.
- **Hand-off to the user's coding agent** (channels / MCP Apps) and an MCP `publish_map` tool for agents that explore on
  their own.
- **Big repos are untested.** The head-start scan reads the whole repo.
- **Next, in order:**
  1. **Run Phase 0 with the integration interviewee:** his real question, illuminate vs "Claude + Mermaid" side by side.
  2. Try illuminate on a real repo, or a fresh Scout copy (`../scout-run`; never `../scout-agent`).
  3. Done 2026-11-03: off-topic questions offer a new map (or an answer in words), plus a map switcher. Next there: a
     routing test of 10–15 real questions with expected routes, run by hand since it uses Claude.
  4. Channels hand-off in Claude Code.
  5. MCP Apps.
- **Later (Phase 3 of the plan):**
  - A fast graph engine with updates on every edit (incremental, LSP-style).
  - Live agent activity on the map.
  - "Working somewhere you haven't explored" and a per-user explored-regions map.
  - "This step was patched 5 times this week" counters. That's the *band-aid detector*, and it needs a time dimension.
```

illuminate now runs as a Claude Code channel. The tests pass, but I haven't tried it in a live Claude Code session: the dev-channels flag is ignored in non-interactive mode, so I can't run it from here. Your first run is the real test.

**How it works**
- A new `illume channel` command is an MCP server that Claude Code starts itself. It runs the existing illuminate server inside it.
- The model calls are swapped for a bridge to the user's own Claude Code session. The map-maker, explainer, fixes and `check()` are unchanged, so nothing reaches the map without passing the check. All model work runs on the user's own sign-in, with no API key.
- **Making a map:** Claude calls `illuminate_map`, the map opens in the browser, and the first piece of work comes back in the tool result. Claude explores, then hands in the map with `illuminate_submit`. If some claims fail the check, the reply asks Claude to fix them, so a map gets made in one turn.
- **Questions on the map:** when someone asks something in the browser, it's pushed into the Claude Code chat as a channel message. Claude fetches it with `illuminate_next` and submits an answer, which shows up on the map.
- **Bad output:** if what Claude hands in doesn't fit the format, the problems go straight back to Claude to fix instead of failing the job. If Claude can't finish, `illuminate_fail` tells the person on the map.
- The old CLI with an API key still works, for Codex and CI.

**To try it**
```
npm i && npm run build
claude mcp add --scope user illuminate -- node "$PWD/packages/server/bin/illuminate.mjs" channel
cd <some repo>    # care-app is a good first one
claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:illuminate
```
Then ask something like "how does X work? draw me a map."

**Tests:** all package tests and typecheck pass. The new `test/channel.test.ts` plays Claude Code's side: it makes a map in one turn, and a question asked on the map is pushed into the chat and answered back on the map. I also started it over real stdio the way Claude Code does, and it connected and listed its tools. A map request is about 3.5k tokens, even on scout-run.

**Gaps you'll notice**
- **Read-only isn't enforced.** Claude uses its own session's tools and permissions, so read-only and "never read secret files" are instructions rather than hard limits. The map is still checked, and fixes are still applied by illuminate only after you approve them.
- **Less progress in the browser.** It says "Claude Code is working on this in your terminal", but no longer shows what Claude is reading.
- **New tab per map.** Each new map opens a new browser tab.
- **The chat has to stay open.** Questions asked on the map wait until Claude finishes what it's doing.
- **Permission prompts.** Each illuminate tool call asks for approval unless the user allows `mcp__illuminate__*`.
- **Team/Enterprise.** On claude.ai Team and Enterprise, an owner has to turn Channels on first.
- **If it doesn't connect,** try the launch with `MCP_SDK_GENERATION=v1` set; that fixed an earlier attempt. This version uses an older protocol that should avoid that problem.

**Other changes:** I updated the README (channel setup first, API-key CLI second), SKILL.md, HANDOFF.md and CLAUDE.md. The CLI help and README no longer suggest handing illuminate to others with a Claude Code sign-in. I also pinned `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` at 1.32.2 as a direct dependency; it was already installed. Nothing is committed.

The new code is in `packages/server/src/channel.ts` and `packages/server/src/bridge.ts`, with small hooks in `server.ts`, `schemas.ts`, `agent.ts`, `maker.ts`, `explainer.ts` and `cli.ts`.
